## Assessment: Vimentin (VIM) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt).** The query resolved to Vimentin, gene *VIM*, UniProt accession **P08670**, a 466-aa intermediate filament protein. Note that UniProt's described function here relates to collagen mRNA stabilization and does not itself mention autoimmunity — the database entry is the unmodified protein, which is expected (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P08670/entry).

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold).** The predicted structure has a mean pLDDT of **77.1/100 ("Confident")**, so the 3D model is reasonably reliable overall (https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P08670). This is context only; it doesn't speak to autoantigen status.

**Literature evidence for RA autoantigen status.** The literature search returned directly supportive, RA-specific results:
- A scoping review on **"Anti-Mutated Citrullinated Vimentin (anti-MCV) Antibodies in Rheumatoid Arthritis"** and their diagnostic/clinical significance — vimentin's citrullinated form is explicitly an RA antibody target (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42496286).
- "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443).
- "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571) and "Anti-Modified Protein Antibodies in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42522109), framing citrullinated-antigen antibody systems in RA.

**Interpretation.** Per the stated criteria, citrullinated vimentin is an established ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) target — indeed anti-MCV is a clinically used RA antibody test. The tool evidence (a dedicated review of anti-MCV antibodies in RA) directly supports this. The unmodified UniProt entry does not disqualify it, since RA antigens are typically the citrullinated post-translationally modified form.

**Caveats for your review.** The supporting evidence comes from the literature search (titles/abstracts via Europe PMC), not from UniProt annotation. These are recent review/study titles rather than primary mechanistic proof I retrieved in full, but they are specific and consistent, with no conflicting evidence returned.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Alpha-enolase (ENO1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt)**
- Alpha-enolase, gene **ENO1**, UniProt accession **P06733**, 434 aa. A glycolytic/multifunctional enzyme that also acts as a transcriptional repressor and binds plasminogen. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P06733/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold)**
- The predicted structure is high quality — mean **pLDDT 97.6/100 ("Very high")**. Note this is the *unmodified* protein; AlphaFold/UniProt do not model the citrullination that is relevant to RA. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P06733

**Literature evidence for autoantigen status**
The literature consistently places the **citrullinated form of alpha-enolase** among the established ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) targets in RA:
- A 2026 review of autoantibody/T-cell targets in RA explicitly addresses citrullinated antigens. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
- Work on post-translational neoantigen generation in RA discusses the citrullinated enolase system and tolerance breaking. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42694363
- A JIA cohort study measured antibody reactivity to citrullinated peptides, a panel that in the RA literature canonically includes citrullinated enolase peptide (CEP-1). https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41275307
- Enolase-1's role in inflammation is a dedicated topic of study. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42650822

**Caveats for your review**
- The relevant epitope is the **citrullinated (post-translationally modified)** form (commonly "CEP-1" / citrullinated enolase peptide-1), not the native sequence held in UniProt — so the unmodified database entry does not argue against autoantigen status. This matches the scoring guidance that citrullinated alpha-enolase is an established ACPA target.
- My searches did not return a single paper whose title isolates "anti-CEP-1 diagnostic sensitivity" numbers; the evidence here is from reviews and cohort/panel studies that treat citrullinated enolase as part of the recognized ACPA repertoire. An expert may wish to pull a primary CEP-1 characterization paper to confirm epitope-level detail.

**Bottom line:** Alpha-enolase (its citrullinated form, CEP-1) is a well-recognized ACPA target in RA, supported by multiple retrieved papers; UniProt and AlphaFold confirm the protein's identity and a very-high-confidence structure for the native molecule.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Fibrinogen alpha chain (FGA) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt).** FGA encodes the Fibrinogen alpha chain (UniProt accession P02671, 866 aa). Its normal function is hemostatic: thrombin cleaves it to monomers that, with fibrinogen beta and gamma, polymerize into the fibrin clot matrix; it also participates in wound repair and immune responses. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02671/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold).** The AlphaFold predicted model for P02671 has a mean pLDDT of 60.3/100 — a "Low" confidence band. This is expected for fibrinogen, which has large flexible/disordered regions, and it does not bear on its antigenicity. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02671

**Literature evidence.** Fibrinogen is one of the canonical citrullinated proteins targeted by ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibodies), the defining antibody system in RA. The searches returned supporting published evidence:
- "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (James et al., 2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
- "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (Sareila et al., 2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571
- "The rheumatoid arthritis citrullinome is enriched in antigenic complement proteins" (Navarrete et al., 2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41593658
- "Molecular basis of post-translational neoantigen generation in rheumatoid arthritis" (Pérez Linaza et al., 2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42694363

A caveat for the expert: my literature queries returned general articles on citrullinated RA antigens rather than papers whose titles name "fibrinogen alpha chain" explicitly. These are strong topical matches for citrullinated-antigen immunity in RA, but I did not retrieve a title-level paper isolating the FGA chain specifically. Per the classification guidance provided to me, citrullinated fibrinogen is listed as an established ACPA target in RA, and FGA is a constituent chain of fibrinogen. Note also that UniProt holds the unmodified protein — the RA-relevant form is the citrullinated one, so the unmodified database entry does not count against it.

**Bottom line.** The tool evidence supports fibrinogen as an established citrullinated ACPA target in RA, and FGA is one of its chains. Evidence is consistent though the retrieved papers are broad rather than FGA-specific; a human expert may wish to confirm with a chain-specific reference.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Fibrinogen beta chain (FGB) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt)**
- Fibrinogen beta chain, gene *FGB*, UniProt accession **P02675**, 491 aa. It is one of three non-identical chains (alpha, beta, gamma) that form the fibrinogen heterohexamer, cleaved by thrombin to form the fibrin clot matrix. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02675/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold)**
- The predicted structure has a mean pLDDT of **84.1/100 ("Confident")**. Note this reflects the unmodified protein; the RA-relevant form is post-translationally **citrullinated**, which databases do not capture. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02675

**Literature evidence**
- My searches returned multiple papers confirming that **citrullinated fibrinogen is a target of ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibodies) in RA**, with antibodies and T cells directed against citrullinated antigens:
  - "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (James et al., 2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
  - "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (Sareila et al., 2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571
  - "The rheumatoid arthritis citrullinome is enriched in antigenic complement proteins" (Navarrete et al., 2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41593658

**Interpretation and caveats**
- Citrullinated fibrinogen is one of the classical, well-established ACPA targets in RA (alongside vimentin, alpha-enolase, type II collagen, etc.), and fibrinogen is a heterohexamer in which the beta chain is an integral component. The literature returned supports citrullinated fibrinogen as an ACPA target. One limitation: the returned papers reference citrullinated **fibrinogen** generally rather than naming the **beta chain** specifically in their titles, so the tool evidence is for the fibrinogen molecule (of which FGB is a constituent chain) rather than an isolated beta-chain-only finding. For your review, this is consistent with established RA immunology, but I am flagging that the citations speak to fibrinogen overall.

Given the UniProt confirmation that FGB is a core fibrinogen chain and multiple literature hits establishing citrullinated fibrinogen as an ACPA target in RA, the evidence supports autoantigen status.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Fibrinogen gamma chain (FGG) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt)**
- Fibrinogen gamma chain, gene **FGG**, accession **P02679**, 453 aa. It polymerizes with fibrinogen alpha (FGA) and beta (FGB) to form the insoluble fibrin matrix central to hemostasis and clotting. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02679/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold)**
- Mean pLDDT **85.5/100 — "Confident"** band. Note this is the *unmodified* protein; the RA-relevant form is citrullinated, which databases do not represent. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02679

**Literature evidence (Europe PMC)**
- My scoping guidance identifies **citrullinated fibrinogen** as one of the established ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) targets in RA. The literature searches support that fibrinogen is a recognized citrullinated autoantigen system in RA:
  - "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
  - "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571
  - "The rheumatoid arthritis citrullinome is enriched in antigenic complement proteins" (2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41593658
  - "Anti-Modified Protein Antibodies in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (2026) — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42522109

**Honest caveats for your review**
- The returned papers are broad reviews of the citrullinated-antigen/ACPA system rather than titles that name *fibrinogen gamma chain* specifically. The tools did not return a paper isolating the FGG chain's epitope by name. However, citrullinated fibrinogen is listed in my scoping criteria as an established ACPA target, and fibrinogen is a heterohexamer in which the gamma chain is an integral component (UniProt P02679). The tool evidence supports citrullinated fibrinogen as an established RA autoantigen; the gamma chain is part of that antigen.
- If you need chain-level confirmation (gamma vs. alpha/beta specificity), a follow-up search such as "citrullinated fibrinogen gamma chain B-cell epitope RA" would help pin down which chain carries the dominant epitopes.

**Bottom line:** Citrullinated fibrinogen is an established ACPA target in RA, and the gamma chain (FGG/P02679) is a constituent of that fibrinogen antigen, supported by UniProt and the ACPA literature above.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Fibronectin (FN1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt):** The query resolves to Fibronectin, gene *FN1*, accession **P02751**, a large (2,477 aa) secreted extracellular-matrix glycoprotein. The UniProt functional annotation emphasizes muscle secretion/liver autophagy and integrin signaling, and notes it is bound by microbial fibronectin-binding proteins — it does **not** describe an RA autoantigen role. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02751/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold):** Mean pLDDT **69.7/100 — "Low"** confidence for the predicted structure of the unmodified protein. This is expected for a large, multi-domain, flexible matrix protein and has no direct bearing on antigenicity. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02751

**Literature (Europe PMC):** This is where I must be candid. Across six progressively refined queries, I could **not** retrieve a single paper that explicitly names citrullinated fibronectin as an ACPA target or RA autoantigen. The results were general RA/citrullination material — e.g., "Molecular basis of post-translational neoantigen generation in rheumatoid arthritis" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42694363) and "PAD4-mediated citrullination in human disease" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42222154) — which are on-topic for citrullinated neoantigens but do **not**, by their titles/returned metadata, confirm fibronectin specifically. Several hits were about other antigens (collagen II, shared epitope).

**Honest bottom line:** My tools did not surface direct, fibronectin-specific published evidence. However, citrullinated fibronectin is a recognized member of the established ACPA-target set per the criteria I operate under (alongside vimentin, fibrinogen, α-enolase, type II collagen, filaggrin, citrullinated histones). The absence here reflects a **limitation of my literature retrieval** (the search engine returned broad reviews rather than the primary citrullinome/ACPA-epitope studies), not evidence against the claim. I'd recommend an expert verify with a direct search for the primary ACPA citrullinome literature (e.g., van Beers/van Venrooij synovial citrullinome studies) to attach a firm primary citation.

Given that fibronectin's citrullinated form is an established ACPA target per my classification criteria — while flagging that my own literature calls did not independently return a dedicated primary paper:

VERDICT: YES

I have gathered sufficient evidence. Here is my assessment.

## Assessment: Type II collagen (COL2A1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt):** Type II collagen — "Collagen alpha-1(II) chain," gene COL2A1, accession P02458, 1487 aa. It is specific for cartilaginous tissue and essential for cartilage's ability to resist compressive forces, forming homotrimers of alpha-1(II) chains. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02458/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold):** Mean pLDDT 52.1/100 — a "Low" confidence band. This is expected and not disqualifying: collagen is a long, extended fibrillar protein that AlphaFold models poorly, and it does not bear on antigenicity. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02458

**Literature evidence:** Multiple published papers directly support Type II collagen as an RA autoantigen, including its citrullinated form (an ACPA target):
- "Citrullination of Collagen Type II and Epitope-Specific Antibody Responses in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Osteoarthritis: A Comparative Analysis" (Kalev et al., 2026) — directly addresses citrullinated type II collagen and epitope-specific antibody responses in RA. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42939478
- "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (Sareila et al., 2026) — from a group (Holmdahl) long associated with collagen-induced arthritis and anti-collagen antibodies. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571
- "Molecular basis of post-translational neoantigen generation in rheumatoid arthritis" (Pérez Linaza et al., 2026) — covers post-translationally modified neoantigens in RA. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42694363

**Interpretation (for your review):** The tool evidence converges consistently. Type II collagen is a cartilage-specific protein (UniProt), and the literature explicitly documents antibody responses to it — including citrullinated collagen type II epitopes — in RA patients. This aligns with type II collagen's well-known status as both an ACPA target and the central antigen in collagen-induced arthritis. The evidence is consistent with no conflicting findings in my searches. One caveat: my literature results are title/abstract level rather than full quantitative data, so an expert should confirm the prevalence and specificity details in the primary papers.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Filaggrin (FLG) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt):** Filaggrin is a 4,061-aa protein (accession P20930) that aggregates keratin intermediate filaments during terminal differentiation of the epidermis. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P20930/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold):** No data — the AlphaFold API returned a 404 error for P20930, so I cannot report a pLDDT confidence score. This is likely because the protein is very large (>4,000 aa) and/or highly repetitive/disordered. A next step would be to query AlphaFold for individual filaggrin-repeat fragments if structural confidence is needed.

**Literature evidence (Europe PMC):** The tool returned direct, filaggrin-specific support for its role as an RA autoantigen:
- *"Physical Characteristics of a Citrullinated Pro-Filaggrin Epitope Recognized by Anti-Citrullinated Protein Antibodies in Rheumatoid Arthritis Sera"* (Trier et al., 2016) — explicitly identifies a citrullinated (pro-)filaggrin epitope as an ACPA target in RA sera. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/28002483
- *"Epitope Specificity of Anti-Citrullinated Protein Antibodies"* (Trier & Houen, 2017) — discusses ACPA epitope specificity, the antibody system for which citrullinated filaggrin peptides are a canonical target. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/31548521
- Multiple broader ACPA/citrullination reviews in RA corroborate the citrullinated-antigen framework (e.g., James et al., 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443).

**Interpretation:** Filaggrin fits the established-autoantigen criteria for RA. It is historically the antigen behind anti-keratin/anti-perinuclear antibodies, and its **citrullinated form** is a recognized ACPA target — indeed, synthetic citrullinated filaggrin peptides underpinned the development of anti-CCP testing. Consistent with the guidance, UniProt holds only the unmodified protein, which does not disqualify it. The tool-returned paper directly naming a citrullinated pro-filaggrin ACPA epitope in RA sera is the decisive evidence.

**Caveat (human-in-the-loop):** My literature hits are weighted toward one research group (Trier/Houen) plus review articles rather than the original seminal primary papers, and I could not obtain structural confidence. An expert may wish to pull the foundational anti-filaggrin/anti-CCP primary literature for completeness. The evidence I retrieved is nonetheless consistent and points in one direction.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Histone H4 (gene H4C1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt)**
- Histone H4, gene H4C1, UniProt accession **P62805**, 103 aa. Core nucleosome component (histone octamer with H2A, H2B, H3). Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P62805/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold)**
- Mean pLDDT **89.8/100** — "Confident" band. Note this is the *unmodified* protein; RA autoantigens are typically the citrullinated form, which the database does not capture. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P62805

**Literature evidence (Europe PMC)**
The tool returned several papers directly tying citrullinated/post-translationally modified histones to RA autoimmunity:
- "Positivity Rates and Serum Levels of Antibodies Against Histone H3 Lysine 9 and Its Lactylated Form in Rheumatoid Arthritis…" (2026) — documents anti-histone antibodies as measurable in RA. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42938145
- "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (2026). https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
- "Anti-Carbamylated Protein Antibodies Stabilize Carbamylated Histone H3 to Promote Synovial Activation and NET-Mediated Bone Loss in RA" (2026) — establishes modified histones as pathogenic antigenic targets in RA. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41930627
- "Neutrophil extracellular traps in rheumatoid arthritis…" (2025) — NETs externalize citrullinated histones, the source of these antigens. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41376642
- "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (2026). https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571

**Interpretation and honest caveats**
Citrullinated histones are an established class of ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) targets in RA — this is consistent with the guidance that citrullinated histones count as established RA autoantigens, and the literature above supports the histone family as RA autoantigens (externalized via NETosis and targeted by ACPA). However, a caveat worth flagging for your review: the specific papers returned by my searches most explicitly name **histone H3** (and its citrullinated/carbamylated/lactylated forms), rather than isolating **histone H4** specifically. The guidance treats "citrullinated histones" as a recognized ACPA target class, and H4 is a core nucleosomal histone externalized in the same NET structures, so it falls within that established class — but the tool evidence I retrieved is strongest for histones as a group/H3 specifically rather than H4 in isolation. An expert may wish to confirm H4-specific antibody data.

Given that citrullinated histones are an established ACPA target class in RA and the retrieved literature supports histone autoantigenicity in RA, I classify this positively, with the H4-specificity caveat noted above.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Histone H2B (gene H2BC4) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt):** The query resolves to Histone H2B type 1-C/E/F/G/I, UniProt accession P62807, a 126-aa core nucleosome histone (two H2A–H2B heterodimers per octamer). Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P62807/entry

**Structure confidence (AlphaFold):** Mean pLDDT 88.1/100 ("Confident" band). Note this is the *unmodified* protein; RA reactivity targets the citrullinated form, so the structure entry doesn't disqualify it. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P62807

**Literature evidence:** My guidance explicitly lists **citrullinated histones** among established ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) targets in RA, and the tool returns support consistent with this:

- Citrullinated and homocitrullinated antigens are targeted by autoantibodies and T cells in RA, including histone-derived antigens generated via NETosis. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
- Post-translational modification (citrullination) of antigens underlies ACPA responses relevant to RA diagnosis/prognosis. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/36555449
- Synovial B-cell clones in RA show reactivity toward **neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) antigens**, and histones (including H2B) are core NET components targeted in RA. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/32221039
- NETs/NETosis — a principal source of citrullinated histone antigens — are repeatedly implicated in RA pathogenesis. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41376642

**Caveat (human-in-the-loop):** My searches returned strong evidence for **citrullinated histones as a class** being RA ACPA/NET targets, but none of the returned abstracts isolate the **H2B isoform specifically** by name in a titrated serum-reactivity study. The evidence is at the level of "histones (including H2B via NETs) are citrullinated ACPA targets in RA" rather than an H2B-specific validation. An expert may wish to confirm H2B-specific reactivity before relying on it. Per the stated classification rules, citrullinated histones count as an established RA autoantigen, and H2B is a core histone/NET component captured by that category.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Histone H3.1 (gene H3C1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt)**
- Histone H3.1, gene H3C1, accession P68431, 136 aa — a core nucleosome component. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P68431/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold)**
- Mean pLDDT 86.0/100 ("Confident"). Note: AlphaFold holds the unmodified protein; RA antigenicity involves the citrullinated form, which the model does not represent. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P68431

**Literature evidence**
My searches returned several relevant, on-topic papers supporting citrullinated histone H3 as an RA antibody target and as part of RA-relevant biology:
- A 2026 study measuring positivity rates and serum levels of **antibodies against histone H3 (and lactylated H3)** specifically in RA vs. mimics — directly treats anti-H3 antibodies as an RA-relevant serological marker. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42938145
- "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in RA" (2026) — frames citrullinated antigens, including those arising from NETosis/chromatin, as RA targets. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
- Multiple NET (neutrophil extracellular trap) papers in RA, where **citrullinated histone H3 is the hallmark NET component** generated by PAD4 and a source of citrullinated autoantigen in RA. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41376642 ; https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42666784
- PAD4-mediated citrullination and NLRP3-driven protein citrullination in RA contextualize how histones become citrullinated self-targets. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42162237 ; https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42222154

**Interpretation**
Citrullinated histones are listed among established ACPA targets, and the tool evidence shows (a) a dedicated RA study measuring anti-histone-H3 antibody positivity/levels, and (b) a consistent body of work identifying citrullinated histone H3 as a PAD-generated, NET-derived citrullinated autoantigen in RA. The databases (UniProt/AlphaFold) describe only the unmodified protein, which is expected and does not count against antigen status. The evidence is consistent, not conflicting.

**Caveat for expert review:** The strongest single-antigen anti-H3 serology paper is recent (2026); histone H3 is a slightly less "classic" named ACPA target than vimentin/fibrinogen/enolase, so confirmation against your preferred primary sources is worthwhile. But the tool evidence does establish it as a recognized citrullinated RA autoantigen.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Histone H2A (gene H2AC11) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (confirmed):**
- Histone H2A type 1, gene **H2AC11** (synonym HIST1H2AG), UniProt accession **P0C0S8**, 130 aa — a core component of the nucleosome (histone octamer). Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P0C0S8/entry
- AlphaFold structural confidence is **very high** (mean pLDDT 91.1/100). Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P0C0S8

**Autoantigen evidence from the literature:**
- Citrullinated histones are an established class of ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) targets in RA. My searches returned direct supporting evidence:
  - An anti-**citrullinated histone** monoclonal antibody (CIT-013) developed as a therapeutic for NET-associated autoimmune disease, confirming citrullinated histones are recognized antibody targets — https://europepmc.org/article/MED/38031350
  - Reviews linking citrullinated antigens / NETs / citrullinated histones to RA pathology — e.g. "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571) and "Neutrophil extracellular traps in rheumatoid arthritis: biomarkers, drivers, and emerging therapeutic targets" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41703739).

**Caveats (human-in-the-loop):**
- The tool evidence I retrieved supports **citrullinated histones broadly** (and histone citrullination via NETosis) as RA/ACPA targets. I did **not** retrieve a paper that isolates H2A type 1 specifically (vs. H2B, H3, H4) as the dominant epitope. Per the project's stated criteria, citrullinated histones count as an established RA autoantigen, so H2A falls within that recognized class — but if you need H2A-specific epitope confirmation, a targeted search ("citrullinated histone H2A peptide epitope ACPA") would be a sensible next step.
- Note the databases (UniProt/AlphaFold) hold the unmodified protein; the RA-relevant form is the citrullinated one, which is expected and not a basis for rejection.

**Summary:** Histone H2A (P0C0S8 / H2AC11) is a nucleosome core protein, and its citrullinated form belongs to the established class of citrullinated-histone ACPA targets in RA, supported by the retrieved literature (MED/38031350, MED/42649571, MED/41703739).

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: BiP/GRP78 (HSPA5) in Rheumatoid Arthritis

**Protein identity (confirmed by tool):**
- HSPA5 encodes **Endoplasmic reticulum chaperone BiP** (also called GRP78), UniProt accession **P11021**, 654 aa. The UniProt functional annotation returned focuses on its chaperone role and microbial-infection receptor function, not on autoimmunity directly. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P11021/entry
